original_proposal.topic: An explicit grant of Elements is repeated, unlike printed margin Elements
original_proposal.proposed_question: A legally used Elemental Boon grants Elements through its effect text. It is then legally Repeated using Powerstorm. Does its explicit Element-grant instruction happen again, and are the card’s printed margin Elements gained again?
original_proposal.predetermined_answer: The explicit Element-grant instruction happens again, so its benefit can be received twice. Repeating does not grant the card’s printed margin Elements again; those were gained when the card was played.
minimum_asked_facts: Repeat resolves the explicit Element-grant effect again.
Printed margin Elements are not gained again.

primary_sources.label: Official FAQ .9v5ka9b: explicit Element-grant text repeats, printed card Elements do not
Original CORE p22 solo rule expressly names Elemental Boon as an ordinary core Power

primary_sources.transcription: Once this turn, target may Repeat a Power Card by paying its cost again.
primary_sources.role: Actual original-core Repeat producer; full native face/no expansion emblem inspected.

actual_prompt_overlap_assessment.literal_ask: do you gain its printed Elements again?
actual_prompt_overlap_assessment.assessment: Only margin Elements are asked. The fixed key adds the explicit-grant exception, but the asked map expressly and correctly classifies that sentence as key_context_not_required.

These ask retained modifiers/current thresholds, flexible-Element choice timing, Power-use/card-play counting, or already-owned Element eligibility. None requests the positive repeated-text grant branch.

original_proposal.why_novel: The official FAQ expressly distinguishes two Element-acquisition mechanisms within the same Repeat ruling. All existing asked facts permit a mistaken blanket rule that repeating can never grant Elements. The new ask isolates the source-defined positive exception, rather than changing a number, a printed payload or adding an arbitrary interaction. Its margin clause is disclosed regression overlap, not second novelty.

scope_assessment.producer_proof: Original CORE p22 identifies Elemental Boon in ordinary solo play; the applicable official FAQ explicitly names it as an Element-grant card whose text can be repeated. The fully viewed original-core Powerstorm supplies Repeat permission. No expansion-named or invented modifier is used.

coverage_decisions.source_correct_answer: Yes. Repeating Elemental Boon resolves its explicit Element-grant instruction again.

key_context_not_required.fact: Powerstorm repayment, printed costs, choice timing, target restrictions, number/types of Elements and threshold numbers.
key_context_not_required.why_not_requested: Legality/producer context or other existing asks; none is a new recital required by this question.

coverage_decisions.refinement: Remove the already-asked printed-margin clause. Keep only the positive repeated text-grant question, with one required fact.
coverage_decisions.source_defined_distinct_procedure: Distinguish Elements obtained from putting a card in play from Elements obtained by resolving an instruction. The official FAQ expressly identifies a positive effect-text grant despite the ordinary no-Elements-on-Repeat statement.
coverage_decisions.why_not_just_repeated_payload: This is the Element-specific boundary of the existing no-Elements rule, not another amount of a generic benefit. Q42’s Energy example does not require applying the positive Element-text branch; Q40 explicitly omits that branch from its asks. The answer is derivable from correct general rules, but the existing required facts do not test this source-defined qualification. No numerical payload, card combination outcome or new repeat count earns credit.

question.question: When a Fast Gift of Strength or Powerstorm grants a Repeat, must the card be chosen immediately? Can the chosen card be Slow, can it be an innate, and do you gain its printed Elements again?

key.answer: Choose eligible Power Card when actually repeating, not necessarily at grant time. Slow cards can be repeated in Slow; these two effects specify cards and cannot repeat Innates. Printed card Elements are not granted again; explicit Elements in the repeated text are granted again.

key.answer: No. Directly gained flexible Elements must be chosen immediately when gained; passive track Any can wait until later in turn, then is fixed for that turn.

question.question: A Spirit plays two Power Cards and later Repeats one. For an effect counting Power Cards played, such as Boon of Vigor, is the count two or three? Does the Repeat consume another ordinary Card Play, and does it nevertheless count as a new Power use?

question.question: A Spirit with no Energy remaining receives Gift of Strength and has already used an eligible cost-1 Power Card. May it use that card's Repeat without paying its cost again, or does Gift require the same repayment as Powerstorm?

key.answer: Yes. The eligible Gift of Strength Repeat can be used with no Energy remaining. Its printed cost limit is an eligibility limit, not a payment instruction. Powerstorm’s separate explicit repayment condition does not apply to Gift.

source_refs.complete_operative_passage:
--- Page 22 ---
GAMEPLAY OPTIONS
SOLO PLAYER MODE
Solo games work much like normal games, but with a single board as the whole Island. The only 
difference is that you can target yourself with Powers that specifically target “Another Spirit”, though 
you do not gain extra benefits from Powers that are better when used on another Spirit, like Gift of 
Constancy or Elemental Boon. Also, the luck of the draw is high, and you have no fellow Spirits to 
compensate for your Spirit’s weaknesses and limitations.

REPEAT
Repeating a Power lets you activate its effect again. It does not give you Elements again (you gain 
Elements for putting a Power Card in play, not for using its effect) and Repeats cannot be chained 
(ignore any “Repeat” effects on a Repeated Power). The Repeated Power is Slow or Fast, whichever 
the original Power is. Here are some additional fine points:
•	 Changes to a Power carry over to the Repeat use. (For instance, if a Power is made Fast or   
 given additional Range, that also applies to the Repeat.)
•	 You may make different choices when Repeating a Power.
•	 If a Repeat specifies where to use it, obey those instructions (instead of the usual Range and  
 Target restrictions). Otherwise, you can choose any valid target by the usual rules, including the  
 same target as its first use.
•	 Repeating a Power Card doesn’t count as playing another Power Card. (For, e.g., Boon of  
 
 Vigor.) It does count as using a new Power. (For, e.g., Bringer of Dream and Nightmares.)

source_refs.complete_operative_passage:
How does one move Presence during Growth?
(.7w4g8oq)
When a Growth choice says "Move Presence" (with a curved arrow), move one of your Presence up to the shown number of lands away from where it currently lies. When the Growth option says "Add Presence", but instead of adding from your Presence track you choose to add one already on the board
(per the p. 14 sidebar)
, you can take it from anywhere. (This is still considered "adding a Presence", not "moving a Presence"; later reprints of the rulebook use the term
repositioning
.)
Ocean's Hungry Grasp also has Growth choices with "Push Presence" and "Gather Presence"; these work just as Gather and Push usually do
(to/from an adjacent land)
. They are mandatory.
(
Discussion elsewhere
(https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1814539/how-do-you-move-presence)
)

source_refs.complete_operative_passage:
When you reposition Presence on the board rather than adding new Presence, where can you measure the range from?
(.bu6od08)
You can measure the range from any Presence, including the one you are about to reposition.
The sequence of events for adding Presence during growth, you
Choose a land to add Presence to. This must be measured from your Presence on the board at that moment.
Add a Presence to that land.
Normally this is picked up from your Presence track, but you can pick it up from anywhere on the island instead if you want. The sequence is similar when a Power lets you add Presence.
(
Discussion elsewhere
(https://boardgamegeek.com/article/28530929#28530929)
)

source_refs.complete_operative_passage:
REPOSITIONING PRESENCE
It is rarely relevant, but whenever you would
add a Presence from your Presence Track,
you may instead use one of your Presence
from anywhere on the Island. This is most
often useful if all your Presence is in play:
you can still reposition it.
